result.title: A Computational Model of Continuous Recognition Memory for Natural Images
result.summary: Recognizing an image we have seen before is a basic function of human visual memory. Understanding human continuous recognition memory (CRM) can help machine vision systems predict which images people are likely to remember and generate more memorable images. It can also inform the diagnosis of memory impairments and the development of interventions to improve memory. This paper proposes the first computational model for CRM. The model captures three key components of continuous recognition memory (CRM): image encoding, memory decay, and decision making. It encodes each image as a distinct random variable in a perceptual space. As the memory of an image fades, the distribution of its random variable drifts within that space. To decide whether the current image has been seen before, the observer retrieves samples from the distributions associated with previously encoded images and compares them with the current image. Our model predicts human observers' trial-by-trial responses in CRM tasks within the variability observed across human participants. Our model is parameter efficient, requiring only four shared parameters and two parameters per observer. It can accurately predict the memorability of an image no worse than prior methods that require millions of parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 提出首个面向自然图像的连续再认记忆计算模型：把每张图像编码为感知空间中的一个随机变量，记忆衰退表现为该分布的空间漂移，判断是否见过时从先前分布采样并与当前图像比较，仅用少量参数即可预测人类逐试次反应。
AI.relevance_reason: 其随机 latent 编码、随时间漂移的记忆状态与「采样—比较」式证据读取，可能为 LVR 中内部状态的保持与衰减、以及答案对 latent 内容的取用方式提供另一种问题表述和评价思路，可供核查迁移性。
